reasons: Claimed status is compliant, and consistent with that no redline or counterparty comment was proposed — the rendered paragraphs are unchanged from the originals, so there is no invalid or directionally wrong edit to assess.

The cited text supports the compliance call: no provision assigns Sanofi (our party) IP, know-how or funded data to RevMed; Section 10.1(a)/p0423 and p0259 push Third Party and subcontractor Program Inventions to the engaging Party (with an irrevocable, perpetual, fully-paid, worldwide sublicensable licence fallback), and Section 6.2/p0339 assigns Regulatory Approvals, INDs and NDAs to Sanofi.

Joint ownership here is not walk-away territory: p0424 gives each Party an unrestricted right to exploit and license Joint Program Technology without accounting or consent, backed by a perpetual, irrevocable, fully-paid, worldwide, sublicensable licence outside the US — i.e. at least the fallback position (perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free, sublicensable use of the collaboration output), so no redline is warranted.
The only licence back to RevMed (p0252) is non-exclusive, royalty-free and limited to performing its own obligations, which does not transfer our rights.
Deterministic check ('no assignment of Customer Data/IP to Vendor remains') passes, corroborating the substantive read.

Minor: the rationale characterises the joint-ownership construct as 'at or above the preferred position' when preferred actually says 'no joint ownership' — it is more accurately a fallback-level outcome. This is a rationale nuance only and does not change the compliant classification. The rationale appropriately flags that the core allocation sentence in 10.1(a) is redacted ([***]) and should be confirmed against the unredacted text before signature.
